title: How shall I put it?
description: How can I express this carefully?
details:
Example: How shall I put it? The room is rather small.

Usage: Conversational; gain time before a delicate statement.

title: Let me think
description: Give me a moment to consider.
details:
Example: Let me think; Tuesday might work.

Usage: Neutral; hold your speaking turn briefly.

title: What I mean is
description: Here is my intended meaning.
details:
Example: What I mean is, we need more time.

Usage: Neutral; clarify your own statement.

title: What I’m trying to say is
description: Here is the point I want to communicate.
details:
Example: What I’m trying to say is, I trust you.

Usage: Neutral; clarify a point you have struggled to express.

title: Let me put it another way
description: I will explain it differently.
details:
Example: Let me put it another way: we’re out of time.

Usage: Neutral; introduce a new formulation.

title: If you see what I mean
description: If my intended idea is clear.
details:
Example: It feels a bit rushed, if you see what I mean.

Usage: Conversational; check understanding indirectly.

title: Do you know what I mean?
description: Do you understand the feeling or idea?
details:
Example: It’s hard to switch off, do you know what I mean?

Usage: Informal; seek shared understanding.

title: You know what?
description: I am about to share a new thought.
details:
Example: You know what? Let’s go for a walk.

Usage: Informal; introduce a spontaneous thought.

title: Come to think of it
description: I have just realised or remembered something.
details:
Example: Come to think of it, I’ve seen that film.

Usage: Conversational; signal a fresh realisation.

title: Speaking of which
description: That connects to another related point.
details:
Example: You mentioned lunch. Speaking of which, are you hungry?

Usage: Neutral; bridge to a related topic.

title: By the way
description: Here is an incidental new topic.
details:
Example: By the way, your parcel arrived.

Usage: Neutral; introduce a side point.

title: While we’re on the subject
description: Before we leave this topic.
details:
Example: While we’re on the subject, how was your interview?

Usage: Neutral; add a related question or point.

title: Anyway, where were we?
description: Let’s return to our interrupted discussion.
details:
Example: Anyway, where were we before the phone rang?

Usage: Conversational; resume after a distraction.

title: As I was saying
description: Returning to my previous point.
details:
Example: As I was saying, we should book early.

Usage: Neutral; can sound pointed after an interruption.

title: Sorry to interrupt
description: Excuse me for speaking before you finish.
details:
Example: Sorry to interrupt, but your taxi is here.

Usage: Neutral; polite interruption.

title: Go on
description: Please continue speaking.
details:
Example: You were saying something about work. Go on.

Usage: Conversational; encourage someone to continue.

title: I’m with you so far
description: I understand up to this point.
details:
Example: I’m with you so far; what happens next?

Usage: Conversational; confirm ongoing comprehension.

title: Could you run that by me again?
description: Please repeat or explain that once more.
details:
Example: Could you run that by me again? I missed the last bit.

Usage: Conversational; politely request repetition.

title: Just to be clear
description: To remove possible misunderstanding.
details:
Example: Just to be clear, we’re meeting at six.

Usage: Neutral; confirm a specific detail.

title: I’ll let you get on
description: I will stop taking up your time.
details:
Example: Thanks for the chat; I’ll let you get on.

Usage: Conversational British usage; politely close a conversation.
